item.title: Additional Tax Revenue Inflow, Ushering in the Era of an 800 Trillion Won Budget Next Year (추가 세수 투입, 내년 ‘예산 800조’ 시대)
item.description:
Additional Tax Revenue Inflow, Ushering in the Era of an 800 Trillion Won Budget Next Year (추가 세수 투입, 내년 ‘예산 800조’ 시대)

The government announced on the 13th that it will draft next year's budget at over 800 trillion won, an increase of more than 10% from this year's 727.9 trillion won. Minister of Strategy and Finance Park Hong-keun stated at the National Fiscal Strategy Meeting held at the presidential office that "for 2027, national tax revenue is expected to reach 500 trillion won plus alpha, the highest ever," adding, "Total expenditure for 2027 will be drafted at 800 trillion won plus alpha, the largest scale ever." <<> President Lee Jae-myung said at the meeting that the additional tax revenue from the semiconductor boom would be used "as strategic investment resources for future preparedness," and "a future response fund will be established to focus investment on four major areas: the future, youth, regions, and education." President Lee remarked, "In times of upheaval, we can either advance or fall off a cliff. The issue is political capability." Despite concerns over increasing national debt due to an aggressive fiscal stance, Minister Park stated, "If you ask whether the country's finances are in good shape, the clear answer is that they are fine." <<> President Lee also said that fiscal resources would be actively invested in the "three mega projects," including the construction of a semiconductor fab in the Honam region, to support the infrastructure needed for semiconductor processes, such as electricity and water supply, stating, "We will mobilize all government capabilities to provide support." In this regard, Minister of Climate, Energy, and Environment Kim Sung-hwan said, "We must significantly increase renewable energy to over 100 GW by 2030 and accelerate the energy transition by harmoniously blending nuclear power," adding, "Whether to introduce new nuclear power plants and small modular reactors (SMRs) will be reflected in the 12th Basic Plan for Power Supply and Demand after public deliberation." <<> Minister of Land, Infrastructure, and Transport Kim Yoon-deok stated regarding the Honam semiconductor industrial complex to be built on the site of the Gwangju military airfield, "We will dramatically shorten the period, which typically takes over 10 years," and "If companies and the Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy request the designation of an industrial complex, we will designate it as a candidate site within one month." Regarding the Yongin semiconductor industrial complex, he said, "We will proceed with consultation and compensation alongside the expropriation and adjudication process to ensure land compensation is completed within the year and construction begins." The Democratic Party of Korea said at a party-government meeting that day that it would not rule out the possibility of building new nuclear power plants and would swiftly enact a "Mega Special Zone Special Act" to support the Honam semiconductor industry, among other initiatives. (정부가 내년도 예산안을 올해(727조9000억원)보다 10% 이상 늘려 800조원대로 편성하겠다고 13일 밝혔다. 박홍근 기획예산처 장관은 이날 청와대에서 열린 국가재정전략회의에서 “2027년도 국세 수입은 500조원 플러스 알파, 사상 최대 세수가 예상된다”며 “2027년도 총 지출은 800조원 플러스 알파, 역대 최대 규모로 편성하겠다”고 말했다.)

item.title: Six Women’s Groups: “Amendment is a Deterioration for Victims… Oppose Abolition of Supplementary Investigation Authority” (여성 6단체 “피해자에 개악… 보완수사권 폐지 반대”)
item.description:
Six Women’s Groups: “Amendment is a Deterioration for Victims… Oppose Abolition of Supplementary Investigation Authority” (여성 6단체 “피해자에 개악… 보완수사권 폐지 반대”)

Women’s groups held a press conference at the National Assembly on the 13th, expressing opposition to the complete abolition of the prosecution’s supplementary investigation authority, led by the Democratic Party of Korea. This comes amid growing calls from within and outside political circles to “reconsider the abolition of the supplementary investigation authority,” spurred by the Jang Yun-gi case in Gwangju, Jeonnam, where police destruction of evidence was uncovered through a prosecution supplementary investigation. Some Democratic Party lawmakers are moving to propose legislation that would retain part of the supplementary investigation authority. However, the Democratic Party leadership maintains its stance as of this day to “pass the amendment to the Criminal Procedure Act for the abolition of the supplementary investigation authority before the party convention in August.” <<> Six women’s groups, including the Korea Sexual Violence Relief Center and the Korean Women’s Association United, expressed concerns at the press conference about the current revision of the Criminal Procedure Act led by the ruling party, stating that “the amendment should not be a deterioration for victims.” The press conference was co-hosted by Democratic Party lawmakers Kim Nam-hee and Kim Dong-ah, as well as Jinbo Party lawmaker Son Sol. Attorney Jeon Da-woon of the Lawyers for a Democratic Society (Minbyeon), who attended the event, stated, “We strongly oppose the complete abolition of the supplementary investigation authority,” and urged, “The National Assembly should halt the hasty rush and pursue responsible reform that guarantees the rights of crime victims.” Choi Seon-hye, Secretary-General of the Korea Women’s Hotline, said, “Victims of violence against women hope for investigations that do not unnecessarily delay and ensure perpetrators face appropriate punishment,” adding, “In this process, substantive supplementation and competition between different agencies are essential.” They also argued that the revision of the Criminal Procedure Act should reflect guarantees of victims’ rights and access to investigation information, as well as the ability to voice opinions. <<> The Democratic Party leadership maintains that “there is no disagreement within the party” regarding the abolition of the supplementary investigation authority. Democratic Party lawmakers on the National Assembly’s Public Administration and Security Committee also refuted claims linking the Jang Yun-gi case to the abolition of the supplementary investigation authority at the press conference that day. Kim Young-jin, the Democratic Party chair of the committee, stated, “The Jang Yun-gi case requires a thorough investigation to clarify the truth, and the supplementary investigation authority is a separate issue to be decided through our discussions,” adding, “Mixing these two issues does little to punish those responsible and uncover the substantive truth.” <<> However, cautious voices within the Democratic Party have grown since the Jang Yun-gi case. The National Assembly’s Legislation and Judiciary Committee held a subcommittee meeting on legislation review on the same day, with only the Democratic Party in attendance from both sides, to continue discussions on the amendment to the Criminal Procedure Act. Reports indicate that there were conflicts even among pro-government lawmakers at the meeting. Recently, the Democratic Party seemed poised to push through the amendment initiated as party policy in the Legislation and Judiciary Committee, but disagreements emerged. One lawmaker reportedly asked the Vice Minister of Justice and the Deputy Chief of the Court Administration Office, “What about an alternative that allows prosecutors to conduct supplementary investigations only when the police fail to comply with a request for supplementary investigation without just cause, and requires them to hand over new criminal facts to the police?” This prompted another lawmaker to retort, “Propose a new bill.” After the meeting, Kim Seung-won, the ruling party secretary on the committee, stated, “We are reviewing the entire criminal justice system from the perspective of protecting citizens’ fundamental rights to ensure it is most efficient and free from grievances.” The Democratic Party decided to hold an assembly of lawmakers on the afternoon of the 14th to discuss differences within the party over the supplementary investigation authority. <<> Democratic Party lawmaker Hong Ki-won, who has advocated for a cautious approach to abolition, sent a private message to all party lawmakers on the 13th, asking them to join the new amendment to the Criminal Procedure Act he proposed. Unlike the party’s official bill, this amendment includes provisions allowing prosecutors to conduct supplementary investigations only for crimes against socially vulnerable groups such as children, the disabled, and the elderly, livelihood crimes like voice phishing, and cases where detention deadlines or statutes of limitations are imminent. An aide to Hong said, “Some lawmakers have already signed on,” and added, “A proposal could be made as early as the 14th.” <<> The People Power Party decided at its assembly of lawmakers on the same day to pursue as party policy a plan to retain the supplementary investigation authority and delay the launch of the Public Prosecution Service and the Major Crimes Investigation Agency by one year. Floor leader Jeong Jeom-sik said at the party meeting, “If the Democratic Party’s current push to dismantle the prosecution and abolish the supplementary investigation authority had been implemented in 1987, the official cause of death for Park Jong-chul would have been ‘cardiac arrest of unknown cause.’” Independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon criticized Democratic Party policy deputy leader Kim Han-gyu’s recent remark that “the Jang Yun-gi case occurred despite the existence of the supplementary investigation authority,” stating, “If the supplementary investigation authority is abolished, more Jang Yun-gi cases will occur, and they will not be caught.” (여성단체들이 13일 국회에서 기자회견을 열어 더불어민주당이 주도하는 검찰 보완수사권 완전 폐지에 반대한다는 뜻을 밝혔다. 경찰의 증거 인멸이 검찰 보완수사로 드러난 전남광주 장윤기 사건을 계기로 정치권 안팎에서 “보완수사권 폐지를 재검토해야 한다”는 주장이 확산되고 있는 것이다. 민주당 일부 의원들은 보완수사권 일부 존치를 위한 법안 발의 움직임을 보이고 있다. 하지만 민주당 지도부는 이날까지도 “8월 전당대회 전 보완수사권 폐지를 위한 형사소송법 개정안을 처리할 것”이란 입장이다.)

item.title: Six pro-Lee members announce bids for top party council; three pro-Chung candidates prepare (친명 6명, 與최고위원 출사표… 친청은 3명 채비)
item.description:
Six pro-Lee members announce bids for top party council; three pro-Chung candidates prepare (친명 6명, 與최고위원 출사표… 친청은 3명 채비)

With the Democratic Party of Korea's leadership race set with five candidates, hopefuls for the Supreme Council positions are steadily announcing their candidacies. In the election to select five Supreme Council members, a total of 12 individuals have so far declared their bids or are seriously considering them. Among them, eight will advance to the primary through a cutoff (preliminary primary) on the 21st. The outcome of this Supreme Council election will determine whether the pro-Lee Jae-myung (친명) or pro-Chung Cheong-rae (친청) faction secures a majority in the next party leadership. <<> The pro-Lee faction has seen a total of six individuals express their intention to run so far. Lawmakers Park Seong-joon, Seo Mi-hwa, and Lee Geon-tae, along with former Deputy Director of the Democratic Research Institute Kim Yong, have announced their candidacies. They are expected to align with former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok. Lawmakers Kim Yeong-ho and Park Seon-won, who are close to pro-Lee lawmaker Song Young-gil, have also thrown their hats into the ring. A key pro-Lee insider remarked, "If multiple candidates from a specific faction run, the vote is likely to split. However, after a round of consolidation through the cutoff, discussions on unification will take place." <<> Within the pro-Chung faction, amid rumors of three potential candidates, Lawmaker Choi Min-hee became the first to officially announce her bid. On the 13th, during an interview on KBS Radio, Choi stated, "I do not engage in line-up politics," while adding, "I agree with former leader Chung Cheong-rae's call for honest politics, swiftly completing reform tasks, and moving toward election victory through the success of a Lee Jae-myung administration." Lawmaker Han Min-soo, who served as Chung's chief of staff during his tenure as party leader, is expected to announce his candidacy on the 14th. Current Supreme Council member Lee Seong-yoon is reportedly deliberating between seeking reelection to the Supreme Council and running for chair of the North Jeolla Provincial Party Committee. Meanwhile, Gwangmyeong Mayor Park Seung-won has also declared his bid for a Supreme Council seat. <<> For the youth Supreme Council position, which the Democratic Party has decided to fill through an election for the first time, former Secretary General of the Military Human Rights Center Kim Hyeong-nam and Deputy Director of the Policy Committee Jeong Min-cheol have expressed their intent to run. However, since the introduction of the youth Supreme Council system would reduce the five Supreme Council seats by one, some candidates are opposing the move, leaving the final decision unresolved. (더불어민주당 당대표 후보는 5명으로 확정된 가운데 최고위원 후보들도 속속 출마 선언을 이어가고 있다. 총 5명을 뽑는 최고위원 선거에는 현재까지 12명이 출마를 선언했거나 유력하게 고심 중이다. 이 중 21일 컷오프(예비 경선)를 통해 8명이 본경선에 진출할 예정이다. 이번 최고위원 선거 결과에 따라 차기 민주당 지도부에서 친명(친이재명), 친청(친정청래) 어느 쪽이 과반을 점할지 결정된다.)

item.title: Jung Cheong-rae Declares Party Leadership Bid, Stating "I Have No Intention of Running for President" (정청래 “대선 나갈 생각 없다” 밝히며 당대표 출마 선언)
item.description:
Jung Cheong-rae Declares Party Leadership Bid, Stating "I Have No Intention of Running for President" (정청래 “대선 나갈 생각 없다” 밝히며 당대표 출마 선언)

Jung Cheong-rae, former leader of the Democratic Party of Korea, officially announced his candidacy for the August 17 party convention on the 13th, saying, "I have no intention of using the party leadership position to run for president." He mentioned not running for the presidency, targeting Kim Min-seok, former Prime Minister and a rival for party leadership as well as a potential next presidential candidate, and lawmaker Song Young-gil. With Jung’s bid for a second term, the party leadership election has become a five-way race among former Prime Minister Kim, lawmaker Song, lawmaker Ko Min-jung, and Kim Bo-mi, former chairwoman of the Gangjin County Council. Two of these candidates will be eliminated through a preliminary primary on the 21st. <<> At a press conference at the National Assembly on the same day, Jung said, "I will not seek personal gain. I will become the strategist for a presidential victory." He added, "I will dedicate everything and devote my life to the re-creation of power, ensuring the stable governance of the Lee Jae-myung administration." This implies that if he becomes the party leader, he will not run for president. This move is interpreted as an attempt to dispel concerns that his bid for re-election as party leader could be seen as a power struggle within the ruling camp over the next presidential candidacy. However, when asked by reporters if this meant he would not run for president even if an opportunity arises, Jung replied, "Please interpret and understand what I said accordingly." <<> In his declaration speech that day, Jung mentioned 'Lee Jae-myung' 30 times and 'reform' 30 times. Notably, he said, "As I have done so far, I will stand by President Lee's side as one team and one voice with the party, government, and presidential office until the end," and "The person who will remain loyal to President Lee until the end is me, Jung Cheong-rae, who has practiced putting the public good before self. Do not worry." He further stated, "The success of the Lee Jae-myung administration, victory in the general election, and the re-creation of power through a presidential election victory are the spirit of the times." Regarding criticisms from some quarters that he was "a party leader who hasn't even had a private meeting with the president," Jung dismissed it as "fake news," saying, "I've met him several times, but just couldn't speak." <<> Jung also said, "I am a single-hearted fool for the Democratic Party," adding, "Since joining the Democratic Party, I have never once left it." This is seen as a jab at former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok, who was at the center of the 'Post-Unification Committee' controversy during the 2002 presidential election, where he advocated for the unification of Roh Moo-hyun, the Democratic Party candidate, and Chung Mong-joon, the candidate of another party. Lawmaker Song Young-gil also left the Democratic Party during the 'envelope of money' incident. <<> Jung, who enjoys support from hardline supporters, continued with strong rhetoric on the same day. He declared, "I will once again become a powerful reformist party leader," and "Prosecution reform is a symbol of Democratic Party reform. I will completely abolish the prosecution's supplementary investigation authority 100%." On the issue of merging with the Fatherland Innovation Party, which he had pursued but suspended due to opposition, he said, "If I become party leader, I will put it to a vote of all party members." Jung also mentioned the 2028 general election, saying, "Specifically, I will strengthen reform nominations in the Honam region." An aide to Jung said, "This heralds a major overhaul of lawmakers from Honam." <<> Former Prime Minister Kim and lawmaker Song directly criticized Jung on the same day, stating, "The party leader must be replaced." Speaking at a joint party member meeting in Anyang, Gyeonggi Province, Kim said, "This party convention is urgent," adding, "If we fail to replace the party leader with the right line and leadership, the party will waver, and the president will also waver." He continued, "I will begin an additive politics that embraces all competent people—reasonable progressives and reformers, reasonable centrists, and reasonable conservatives—to firmly build, expand, and grow the party." Kim also said, "I will be a definite partner for the president and surely lead the party to victory in the general election." <<> Lawmaker Song also appeared on YouTube, saying, "Where in the constitutional history of South Korea has there been a situation where, with a president who still has four years left in office, the ruling party leader and the president are fighting in a 'Myung-Cheong showdown'?" He added, "Jung says there's no showdown, claiming he's wronged, but that's like covering the sky with the palm of your hand," and "What makes him think he's protecting President Lee?" He further remarked, "To protect the president, we need to win the general election. Do you think Jung Cheong-rae's face can win the general election? If he leads the Democratic Party with that face, I think even my son and daughter wouldn't vote for him." (더불어민주당 정청래 전 대표가 13일 “당 대표직을 이용해 대선에 출마할 생각이 없다”며 8·17 전당대회 출마를 공식 선언했다. 당권 경쟁자이자 차기 대선 주자로 거론되는 김민석 전 국무총리, 송영길 의원을 겨냥하며 대선 불출마를 언급한 것이다. 정 전 대표의 연임 도전으로 당대표 선거는 김 전 총리, 송 의원, 고민정 의원, 김보미 전 강진군의회 의장 간 5파전으로 치러지게 됐다. 이들 중 2명은 오는 21일 컷오프(예비경선)를 통해 떨어진다.)

item.title: US Army Recommended Books Focus on 'International Politics and Operations'... South Korea Recommends 'The Analects' and 'Mencius' (美 육군 권장 도서는 ‘국제정치·작전’… 한국은 논어·맹자)
item.description:
US Army Recommended Books Focus on 'International Politics and Operations'... South Korea Recommends 'The Analects' and 'Mencius' (美 육군 권장 도서는 ‘국제정치·작전’… 한국은 논어·맹자)

Minister of National Defense Ahn Kyu-baek recently presented 12 books for military commanders as 'required reading,' primarily consisting of Eastern and Western classics including The Analects, Mencius, and The Admonitions on Governing the People. Within the military, reactions have emerged stating that these books "fail to reflect the rapidly changing security environment of the 21st century and are out of touch with reality." <<> According to a comprehensive report from this outlet on the 13th, Minister Ahn, through the Defense Daily last month, recommended books for commanders such as The Art of War, The Analects, Mencius, Han Feizi, The War Diary of Admiral Yi Sun-sin, The Admonitions on Governing the People, The Book of Corrections, and Baekbeom Ilji. The list also included 'On War' by Prussian war theorist Carl von Clausewitz, 'The Great Philosophers' by German philosopher Karl Jaspers, 'The Importance of Living' by Chinese novelist Lin Yutang, and 'When a Leaf Trembles' by critic Lee Eo-ryeong. <<> Since Minister Ahn took office, the Ministry of National Defense has been promoting the 'One Hand on the Gun, One Hand on the Book' project, emphasizing the need to increase reading among soldiers. The selection of these required readings for commanders is said to be based on the idea that leaders should read first. However, within the military, there are criticisms that "the list leans heavily on classics and general education books, differing greatly from the US military's recommended reading list for officers, which is directly linked to modern defense strategies and tactics." <<> The US Army's 'US Army Chief of Staff's Reading List' from 2017 included over 110 books covering diverse fields such as international politics, geopolitics, and US military operational history. These include 'World Order' by international politics expert Henry Kissinger, 'The Tragedy of Great Power Politics' by realist international relations scholar John Mearsheimer, 'The Future of Power' by Joseph Nye, who first coined the concept of soft power, and 'The Accidental Superpower' by geopolitical strategist Peter Zeihan. There were also titles like 'The Soldier and the State' by Samuel Huntington, which argues that military professionalism and autonomy ensure political neutrality, and 'Fiasco' by Thomas E. Ricks, which sharply criticizes the US military's overall failures during the Iraq War that began in 2003. <<> Publishing critic Pyo Jeong-hoon commented, "While the US military's recommended books focus on global affairs, security environments, and macro-level strategies, our recommended books lean towards classics and do not consider the intended readership of 'military commanders'." He added, "It is regrettable that there is no consideration for books that can provide specific insights into the rapidly changing security environment and international situation." (안규백 국방부 장관이 최근 군 지휘관 ‘필독서’로 논어·맹자·목민심서를 비롯한 동·서양 고전 위주의 책 12권을 제시했다. 군에서는 “21세기 급변하는 안보환경 변화를 전혀 반영하지 않은 책들로, 현실과 동떨어져 있다”는 반응이 나온다.)

item.title: [Episode 25] Sariel's Dilemma ([25화] 사리엘의 딜레마)
item.description:
[Episode 25] Sariel's Dilemma ([25화] 사리엘의 딜레마)

☞ View from Episode 1 (☞ 1화부터 보기)

☞ Character Introductions (☞ 등장인물 소개)

A month had already passed since the introduction of Sariel. As the emergence of this unprecedented artificial intelligence began to tip the balance of power in Northeast Asia, China actively launched a public opinion campaign, sparking heated debates across all sectors of society. (사리엘을 도입한 지 어느덧 한 달이 흘렀다. 전대미문의 성능을 지닌 인공지능의 등장으로 동북아 균형의 추가 한쪽으로 기울기 시작하자, 중국은 적극적으로 여론전에 나섰고, 그 결과 각계각층에서 갑론을박이 일었다.)

"Big Brother Out! Firmly Oppose Deploying Sariel!" (“빅 브라더 아웃! 사리엘 배치 결사 반대!”)

As Director Park Gwan-gyu's official vehicle passed Samgakji and turned onto Gwanghwamun Avenue, the shouts of the protesters penetrated even the sealed-off interior of the car. (박관규 실장의 관용차가 삼각지를 지나 광화문 대로변으로 접어들자 시위대의 고함이 밀폐된 차 안까지 파고들었다.)

In front of the embassy to the United States, red protest slogans were visible among grotesque eyeball placards reminiscent of George Orwell's Big Brother. (주미 대사관 앞엔 조지 오웰의 빅 브라더를 연상시키는 기괴한 눈알 피켓들 사이로 붉은 구호가 보였다.)

"We'll get crushed like shrimp in a fight between the US and China!" (“미국과 중국 싸움에 새우등 터진다!”)

On the opposite side, the area occupied by conservative groups had a completely different atmosphere. Through the left window, the sky was covered with a mix of the American and South Korean flags. Chants boomed from a large amplifier. (반대편 보수 단체의 구역은 전혀 다른 공기였다. 차창 왼쪽에서는 성조기와 태극기가 뒤섞여 하늘을 덮었다. 대형 앰프를 타고 구호가 울려 퍼졌다.)

"Welcome Sariel! God Save Korea!" (“사리엘 배치 환영! God Save Korea!”)

Director Park narrowed his eyes as he crossed through the divided demonstrations. (박 실장은 양쪽으로 갈라진 시위대를 가로지르며 눈을 가늘게 찌푸렸다.)

In the midst of tension stretching taut like a bowstring, his worries lay elsewhere. (팽팽하게 당겨진 활시위 같은 긴장 한복판에서, 그의 걱정은 다른 곳에 머물렀다.)

"If the US remotely shuts down Sariel in an emergency, how will our military respond?" (“유사시 미국이 원격으로 사리엘을 꺼버리면, 우리 군은 어떻게 대응할 것인가.”)

Director Park recalled the kill switch issue that Representative Jin Du-seong had persistently brought up during a recent closed-door parliamentary briefing. At the time, Director Park had pacified the lawmakers by citing the contract terms designed by Evan. (박 실장은 얼마 전 국회 비공개 간담회에서 진두성 의원이 물고 늘어졌던 킬스위치 이슈를 떠올렸다. 당시 박 실장은 에반이 설계한 계약 조항을 근거로 의원들을 잠재웠다.)

"To deactivate Sariel, the system is designed with a triple-lock structure requiring the South Korean government, the US government, and the United Nations Command to input their cryptographic keys simultaneously." (“사리엘을 비활성화하려면 한국 정부, 미국 정부, 유엔군 세 주체가 동시에 암호키를 입력해야 하는 트리플 락 구조로 설계되어 있습니다.”)

He explained that unilateral deactivation was impossible, and that safeguards had been put in place to demand astronomical compensation from Dudael if they violated the terms. (그는 독단적 비활성화는 불가능하며, 듀다엘이 이를 어길 시 천문학적 배상을 요구할 수 있는 안전장치를 마련했다고 설명했다.)

A few lawmakers followed up with additional questions, but those concerns did not leak out of the conference room. (몇몇 의원이 추가 질문을 이어 갔지만, 그 우려가 회의실 밖으로 새어 나오지는 않았다.)

Yet, a lingering unease remained in Director Park's mind. (하지만 박 실장의 마음 한구석에는 찜찜함이 남았다.)

The requirement for consensus among three parties meant, conversely, that the South Korean government could not independently shut down the system on its own territory. (세 주체의 합의가 필요하다는 말은, 뒤집어 말하면 우리 영토 내 시스템을 한국 정부가 독자적으로는 끌 수조차 없다는 뜻이었다.)

Whether it was a shield or a shackle designed by Dudael, his doubts were not entirely dispelled. (방패인지, 듀다엘이 설계한 족쇄인지, 그 의구심이 말끔히 지워지지는 않았다.)

Director Park's official vehicle passed through the main gate of the presidential office, Cheong Wa Dae. After getting out of the car, Director Park headed not to the main building but to the left annex. (박 실장의 관용차 청와대 정문을 통과했다. 차에서 내린 박 실장은 본관이 아닌 왼쪽 별관으로 향했다.)

The aftermath of Sariel's introduction had already deeply permeated the government. Upon entering the annex, three secretaries from the National Security Office and three secretaries from the Office of the Senior Secretary to the President for Economic Affairs were seated on opposite sides of a table, glaring at each other. (사리엘 도입의 후폭풍은 이미 정부 깊숙이 스며들었다. 별관에 들어서자 국가안보실 비서관 3명과 경제수석실 비서관 3명이 테이블 양옆에 갈라져 앉아 서로를 노려보는 중이었다.)

Even before the Prime Minister could take his seat at the head of the table, a free-for-all discussion erupted. (국무총리가 상석에 앉기도 전에, 난상 토론이 벌어졌다.)

"National Security Office, can you take responsibility for this situation?" (“안보실, 지금 이 사태 책임질 수 있습니까?”)

An agitated secretary from the Economic Affairs Office opened fire, throwing a stack of documents onto the table. (흥분한 한 경제수석실 비서관이 서류 뭉치를 테이블에 내동댕이치며 포문을 열었다.)

"China's retaliation has crossed the line. The rare earth export controls are a card they always pull, but this time they're threatening to shut down our company's semiconductor plant in Shenyang as well." (“중국의 보복이 선을 넘었습니다. 희토류 수출 통제야 맨날 나오는 카드라지만, 이번엔 우리 기업의 셴양 반도체 공장까지 폐쇄하겠다고 으름장을 놓고 있어요.”)

"What does that have to do with Sariel?" (“그게 사리엘이랑 어떤 관계가 있습니까.”)

"They're using environmental regulations as a pretext, but the reason is obvious. Our companies are on the verge of collapse just to pinpoint one missile coordinate. Take a look at today's stock prices and exchange rates." (“환경 규제를 빌미로 삼고 있지만, 이유야 뻔하지 않습니까. 미사일 좌표 하나 찍자고 우리 기업들이 다 죽게 생겼단 말입니다. 오늘 주가랑 환율 꼴을 좀 보십시오.”)

"This isn't a simple business matter," retorted the National Security Office secretary. (“이건 단순한 비즈니스가 아닙니다.” 안보실 비서관이 맞받았다.)

"Sariel is a national security project personally decided by the President. Is a few percent drop in the stock index more important than North Korean troops crossing over an empty forward outpost?" (“사리엘은 VIP께서 직접 결단하신 안보 사업입니다. 텅 빈 전방 초소 너머로 북한군이 넘어오는 것보다, 주가 지수 몇 퍼센트 하락하는 게 더 중요합니까?”)

"This is exactly why we're getting this much flak from the public—for belittling the economy." (“경제를 우습게 아니 이렇게 국민들한테 욕을 먹는 겁니다.”)

As voices rose, the Economic Affairs Office secretary shot a glare at Director Park. (고성이 오가는 가운데 경제수석실 비서관이 박 실장을 쏘아봤다.)

"Director of the Strategic Resources Office from the Ministry of National Defense, let me ask you. How can you prove in this very seat that this American-made AI called Sariel is more valuable than the livelihood of our people?" (“국방부에서 오신 전략자원실장님, 묻겠습니다. 저 사리엘이라는 미국산 인공지능이 우리 국민의 먹고사는 문제보다 더 가치 있다는 걸, 이 자리에서 어떻게 증명하시겠습니까?”)

Director Park stared at the yellowing tea bag in his cup, then slowly raised his head. (박 실장은 누렇게 변해가는 찻잔 속 티백을 응시하다가 천천히 고개를 들었다.)

"The Economic Affairs Office has a point. But my thoughts are a little different. Holes in the economy can be filled with sweat, but holes in national security can only be filled with blood." (“경제수석실 말씀도 일리가 있습니다. 하지만 제 생각은 조금 다릅니다. 경제의 구멍은 땀으로 메울 수 있지만, 안보의 구멍은 오직 피로만 메울 수 있습니다.”)

His voice was low, but the noise in the conference room fell silent instantly. (목소리는 낮았지만 회의실의 소음이 단번에 잠겼다.)

Director Park pulled a report stamped with Top Secret from his jacket and placed it on the table. (박 실장이 품 안에서 1급 기밀 도장이 찍힌 보고서를 꺼내 테이블 위에 올렸다.)

"Just two days ago, five small North Korean drones attempted to infiltrate south across the western front of the DMZ. Under the existing radar systems, they would have been mistaken for a flock of birds or not even detected at all." (“불과 이틀 전, DMZ 서부 전선에서 북한군 소형 무인기 5대가 남파를 시도했습니다. 기존 레이더였다면 새 떼로 오인하거나 감지조차 못했을 상황이었습니다.”)

This was the first time those present had heard of this. Everyone's eyes fixed on the report. (이 자리에서 처음 듣는 내용이었다. 좌중의 시선이 보고서에 꽂혔다.)

"Sariel immediately detected them, identified them as a swarm of drones, and automatically recommended a jamming attack. Our military executed countermeasures based on Sariel's assessment." (“사리엘은 즉각 이를 포착해 군집 드론임을 식별했고, 자동으로 재밍 공격을 권고했습니다. 우리 군은 사리엘의 판단에 따라 대응 조치를 실시했습니다.”)

Director Park opened the report. His gaze settled on the vivid photos of the wreckage of the downed North Korean drones. (박 실장이 보고서를 펼쳤다. 그의 시선이 추락한 북한 무인기 잔해의 선명한 사진을 향했다.)

"All of the North Korean drones crashed before even crossing the Military Demarcation Line. Considering the repercussions of publicizing this, it was kept classified. But Sariel, even without our knowledge, has been effectively preventing security gaps in real combat more effectively than any other means." (“북한 측 무인기는 군사분계선을 넘기도 전에 전량 추락했습니다. 이를 공개함에 있어 파장을 고려해 비공개에 부쳤습니다만, 사리엘은 이미 우리가 인지하지 못하는 사이에도 실전에서 안보 공백을 그 어떤 수단보다 효과적으로 막아내고 있습니다.”)

Director Park looked squarely at the Economic Affairs Office secretary. (박 실장이 경제수석실 비서관을 똑바로 봤다.)

"The reason we can sit in this conference room worrying about stock prices is that, even at this very moment, Sariel is quietly preventing war in places unseen. The value of a weapons system is not proven through argument but confirmed through results." (“우리가 주식 걱정을 하며 이 회의실에 앉아 있을 수 있는 건, 지금 이 순간에도 사리엘이 보이지 않는 곳에서 조용히 전쟁을 막고 있기 때문입니다. 무기 체계의 가치는 증명하는 것이 아니라, 결과로 확인하는 것입니다.”)

A moment of silence followed. (잠시 침묵이 흘렀다.)

"First, let's all calm down... We'll need to monitor the situation closely going forward." The Prime Minister wrapped up the meeting, easing the tension on both sides. (“일단, 진정들 하시고… 향후 면밀하게 상황을 모니터링할 필요가 있겠습니다." 국무총리가 회의를 정리하며 양측의 흥분을 가라앉혔다.)

Director Park thought he had barely managed to quell the opposition's voices in the noisy conference room. (박 실장은 소란스러운 회의실에서 간신히 반대파의 목소리를 잠재웠다고 생각했다.)

But the place where those opposing Sariel were quietly preparing their counterattack was not Seoul, but somewhere entirely different. (하지만 사리엘을 반대하는 자들이 조용히 반격을 준비하는 곳은, 서울이 아닌 전혀 다른 곳이었다.)

item.title: "A Paltry Turnout: Only Lee Min-woo and Lee Ki-taek Showed Up" — The First Steps of the 'National Council for Democracy' (“이민우·이기택만 오다니, 한심하다“… ‘민주국민협의회’의 첫 발)
item.description:
"A Paltry Turnout: Only Lee Min-woo and Lee Ki-taek Showed Up" — The First Steps of the 'National Council for Democracy' (“이민우·이기택만 오다니, 한심하다“… ‘민주국민협의회’의 첫 발)

After ending his 23-day hunger strike and being released from house arrest, YS gradually expanded his range of activities. He met with former President Yun Bo-seon and Cardinal Kim Su-hwan to discuss the state of affairs. He visited dissident figures such as Reverend Moon Ik-hwan and Ham Seok-heon to deliberate on the formation of the 'National Council for Democracy,' a pro-democracy opposition group. Through this process, the following year on May 18, 1984, he launched the Council for the Promotion of Democracy (Minchuhyeop). (YS는 23일간의 단식을 끝내고 가택연금이 해제된 상태에서 활동 범위를 점차 넓혔습니다. 윤보선 전 대통령, 김수환 추기경 등을 만나 시국 이야기를 나눕니다. 문익환 목사, 함석헌씨 등 재야 인사를 찾아가 민주화 추진 야권 단체인 ‘민주국민협의회’를 논의합니다. 이 과정을 통해 이듬해 1984년 5월 18일 민주화추진협의회(민추협)를 발족합니다.)

For the first time since his house arrest, he also attended church. While joining a gathering of families of political prisoners, he shed tears. He also conducted interviews with domestic and international media. (가택연금 후 처음으로 교회에도 나갔습니다. 양심범 가족 모임과 함께하면서 눈물도 흘렸습니다. 국내외 언론과 만나 인터뷰도 진행합니다.)

Not everything went as planned. A meeting of opposition leaders was held at the home of his close aide, lawmaker Kim Dong-young, but the turnout was smaller than expected. YS lamented, "Only Vice Chairmen Lee Min-woo and Lee Ki-taek came, had a chat, and left. It’s pathetic. Truly pitiful and frustrating." (모든 일이 뜻대로 되지는 않았습니다. 측근 김동영 의원 집에서 야당 수뇌 모임을 가졌는데 예상보다 참석자가 많지 않았습니다. YS는 탄식합니다. “이민우·이기택 부총재만 와서 이야기하다가 왔다. 한심한 일이다. 정말 불쌍하고 답답한 일이다.”)

This year, the rainy season seems to have arrived early. It started raining the day before yesterday. Since yesterday, strong winds have begun to blow, and the rain has intensified. It seems heavy downpours are hitting somewhere. Thunder and lightning are raging fiercely. (금년(今年)에는 장마가 일찍이 찾아온 것 같다. 그저께부터 비가 오기 시작한다. 어제부터는 몹시 바람이 불기 시작하면서 비도 많이 시작한다. 어디엔가는 폭우가 오고 있는 것 같다. 뇌성벼락이 몹시 치기 시작한다.)

Today is Sunday. After a long time—one year and one month, or 14 months—I was able to attend church. For the first time, an announcement was made at church, and Elder (Woo Jang-no) offered a prayer. (오늘은 주일(主日)이다. 오랜만에 그것도 1년(年)하고도 1개월(個月), 그러니까 14개월(個月)만에 교회(敎会)에 나갈 수 있었다. 처음으로 교회에서 광고(廣告)도 하고 장로(長老)님(우장노)이 기도도 해주었다.)

Many church members waited and lingered outside to catch a glimpse of me as I left. They are truly grateful people. (많은 교우(敎友)들이 나를 보기 위해서 교회(敎會)에서 나올 때 지키고 기다리고 있다. 고마운 분들이다.)

After a long while, Miae came by after finishing her teaching practicum, and we had lunch together. (오랜만에 교생실습이 끝나고 미애가 와서 같이 점심을 먹었다.)

Gang Shin-myeong from the mountaineering club, along with Kim Gyeong-yun from Gyeongsan (a comrade from the southeast region) and my brother-in-law’s elder brother and his wife, visited. Lawmaker Hwang Myeong-su apparently stopped by, but I missed him. (산악회(山岳会)의 강신명씨와 강원도(江原道)에서 남동지 경산의 김경윤 그리고 신서방의 형(兄)님과 형(兄)수가 다녀갔다. 황명수(黃明秀) 의원(議員)이 다녀갔다고 하는데 맞(*만)나지 못했다.)

Kim Yeong-bae and Hwang Byeong-u came by, and we had lunch together while chatting. (김영배(金令培), 황병(黃炳)우가 찾아와서 같이 점심을 먹어(*으)며 이야기를 나누웠(*었)다.)

A reporter from Britain's *The Times* came directly from England for an interview. It’s said to be slated for a special feature next Sunday. (영국(英囗)의 The Time 기자(記者)가 영국(英囗)에서 직접(直接) 와서 회견(會見)을 했다. 내주일(來週日)에 특(特)집으로 발관(*간)된다고 한다.)

In the afternoon, I visited Mr. Yun Bo-seon. I was truly astonished by his views on the current political situation. However, we talked for two hours. I can only be amazed at the difference in our perspectives on the state of affairs. (오후(午后)에는 윤(尹)보선 씨(氏)를 방문(訪問)했다. 정말 시국관(時局觀)에 대(対)해서 놀랬다. 그러나 두 시간(時間) 동안 이야기를 했다. 시국관(時局觀)의 차이에 대(対)해서 놀랠 뿐이다.)

When I returned home, Hong Il, Park Jong-yun, lawyer Kim Myeong-yun, Lee Yong-deok of *The Chosun Ilbo*, and another reporter were waiting. In the evening, I went to Director Kim’s house and then came back. (집에 돌아 왔더니 홍일(弘一), 박(朴)종윤, 김명윤 변호사 조선일보(朝鮮日報)의 이용덕과 또 한 사람의 기자(記者)가 찾아왔다. 저녁에 김실장(金室長) 집에 갔다가 왔다.)

Yesterday, it was just sweltering without any rain, but today, though not heavy, a drizzle is falling. It seems the full rainy season has set in. (어제는 날씨 무덥기만 하고 비는 오지 않았는데 오늘은 많은 비는 오지 않지마는 가랑비가 내고이고(*내리고) 있다. 완전한 장마철에 접어들은(*접어든) 것 같다.)

Choi Hyeong-u, Kim Dong-young, Mun Bu-sik, Jeong Jae-won, and others visited. Kwon Hyeok-chung came by and left. (최형우(崔炯佑), 김동영(金東英), 문부식(文富植), 정재원(鄭在原) 등(等)이 다녀갔다. 권(權)혁충(忠)이가 왔다가 갔다.)

At 3 p.m., I visited Cardinal Kim Su-hwan and talked about the state of affairs for 1 hour and 10 minutes. Though a priest, he is well-versed in everything regarding the current political situation. (오후(午后) 3시(時)에는 김수환(金壽煥) 추기경을 방문(訪問)하고 1시간(時間) 10분(分) 동(*안) 시국(時局)에 대(対)한 이야기를 했다. 사제이지마는 시국(時局)에 대(対)해서 모든 것을 잘 알고 있다.)

I am truly worried about the future of this country. In the evening, General Park Gyeong-won came by. (정말 나라의 장래에 대(対)해서 걱정이다. 저녁에 박경원(朴敬遠) 장군(將軍)이 다녀갔다.)

Many people visited today as well. (오늘도 많은 사람들이 찾아왔다.)

After a long time, I had conversations with many people. I had lunch with Vice Chairman Lee Min-woo and talked at length. (오랜만에 많은 사람들과 대화(對話)를 했다. 이민우(李敏雨) 부총재(副總裁)와 점심을 같이하며 많은 이야기를 했다.)

In the afternoon, I went to Reverend Moon Ik-hwan’s home and spent three hours discussing the future of Korea and the National Council for Democracy. (오후(午后)에 문익환(文益煥) 목사(牧師)를 집으로 찾아가 3시간(時間)동안 한국(韓囗)의 장래(將來)와 민주국민협의회(民主囗民協議会)에 대(対)해서 이야기를 나누웠(*었)다.)

Around 6:30 p.m., I returned home to find a second secretary from the U.S. Embassy waiting, who had been there since 6 p.m. He came to deliver a letter from Congressman Kennedy. (6시(時)30분경(分頃)에 집으로 돌아오니 미국대사관(美囗大使館)에서 이등(二等) 서기관(書記官) 한 사람이 6시(時)부터 찾아와서 기다리고 있다. Kennedy 의원(議員)의 편지를 전달하기 위해서 찾아왔다.)

Late in the evening, Jong-hwak and his wife, along with Seong-hwan from Busan, visited. (저녁 늦게는 종(鍾)확이 부부(夫婦)와 부산(釜山)에서 성환이가 찾아왔다.)

Early in the morning, I received a phone call from a Korean-American daily newspaper in the U.S. (an overseas Korean newspaper). They asked me to deliver a congratulatory message for the first anniversary on July 8, which I did. (아침에 일찌기 미국(美囗)의 매일신문(每日新聞)(교포신문)에 전화가 와서 7월(月)8일(日)이 일주년(一週年)이 된다 축사(祝辭)를 해달라고 해서 이야기를 해주었다.)

Hwang Nak-ju, the general affairs director, came by in the morning, chatted, and left. (황낙주(黃珞周) 총무(總務)가 아침에 와서 이야기를 하다가 갔다.)

I left at 10 a.m. to go to Oksung Pavilion in Uidong for a celebration of Yun Je-sul’s 80th birthday. About 300 to 400 people had gathered. (아침 10시(時)에 떠나서 우이동 옥류장에 가서 윤제술(尹済述)씨(氏)의 8순(旬) 축하연(祝賀宴)에 갔었다. 3~4백명의 사람들이 모여들었다.)

After a long time, I met Yun Je-sul, and I also met many old comrades. They asked me to give a congratulatory speech, which I delivered. After a simple lunch, I returned. (오랜만에 운제도 맞(*만)났지마는 옛날 사람들 많은 동지(同志)들을 맞(*만)났다. 축사(祝辭)를 해달라고 해서 축사(祝辭)를 했다. 점심까지 간단히 먹고 돌아왔다.)

I stopped by lawmaker Kim Dong-young’s house and spent over two hours discussing the National Council for Democracy with Mr. Lee Min-woo before leaving. We engaged in a serious and thorough review. I believe this must be pursued not for personal motives but with an open mind for the democracy of our homeland. (김동영(金東英) 의원(議員) 집에 들여(*려) 두 시간(時間) 이상(以上) 이민우(李敏雨)씨와 민주국민협의회(民主囗民協議会)에 대(対)해서 이야기를 나누다가 왔다. 여러 면으로 진지하게 검투(*토)를 해보았다. 그것은 어디까지나 사사(私私)로운 것이 아니고 조국(祖國)의 민주화(民主化)를 위하여 허심탄헤(*회) 하게 나가야 한다고 생각한다.)

During the day, Jin Kim from the U.S. came by, and we had lunch together while talking. He said he had signed a contract to export $5 million worth of flowers from Korea to the U.S. annually. (낮에는 미국(美囗)의 Jin Kim이 왔어(*와서) 이야기를 하며 점심을 같이 먹었다. 앞으로 한국(韓囗)에서 1년(年)에 500만불(万弗)어치 꽃을 미국(美囗)으로 수출(輸出)하기로 계약을 했다고 한다.)

Last year, the Netherlands imported $8 million worth of flowers from the U.S., and this year they plan to import $10 million worth—he seems to be a considerable businessman. (작년(昨年) ‘네드란드(*네덜란드)’에서 800만불(万弗)어치의 꽃을 미국(美囗)으로 수입(輸入)했고 금년(今年)에는 1000만불(万弗)어치의 꽃을 수입(輸入)할 예정(豫定)이라고 상당(相当)한 사업가(事業家)라고 생각된다.)

I visited Mr. Ham Seok-heon and had a talk, and I went to see Professor Lee Mun-yeong, but only his wife and mother were there. (함석현(*헌)씨(氏)를 방문(訪問)했어(*해서) 이야기를 했고 이문영 교수(敎授)를 찾아갔지마는 부인과 어머님만 맞(*만)났다.)

In the evening, Miae’s parents joined my family for dinner at the Diplomatic Club. Her father seems like a very good person, and her mother as well. I think it’s good that even though we should have met earlier, it wasn’t awkward at all. (저녁에는 ‘미예’ 부모(父母)님을 우리 가족(家族)과 함께 외교(外交)크랍(*클럽)에서 저녁 식사(食事)를 같이 했다. 아버님도 아주 좋은 분이고 어머님도 매우 좋은 분이라고 생각된다. 벌써 맞(*만)나야 하는 것인데 늦었지마는 그렇게 서먹서먹하지 않으(*아)서 좋다고 생각된다.)

This morning, AP came by and took various types of photos. I believe they will be quite meaningful. They took individual shots, as well as family photos. (오늘 아침에는 AP에서 와서 아침에 사진을 여러가지 형태(形態)의 사진을 찍었다. 상당(相当)이 의미(意味)있는 사진이 될 줄 믿는다. 독(獨)사진도 찍었지마는 가족(家族)사진도 함께 찍었다.)

I had lunch accompanied by conversation with Hong Il. In the afternoon, I visited Yeo Chun-ho’s house and talked for over an hour. (점심은 홍일(弘一)이와 같이 이야기를 하면서 했다. 오후(午后)에는 여춘(呂春)호 집을 방문(訪問)해서 1시간(時間) 이상(以上) 이야기를 했다.)

In the evening, at lawmaker Kim Dong-young’s house, we hosted an invitation for the vice chairmen and lawmaker Kim Nok-yeong, but only Vice Chairmen Lee Min-woo and Lee Ki-taek showed up, had a chat, and left. It’s pathetic. Truly pitiful and frustrating. (저녁에는 김동영(金東英) 의원(議員) 집에서 부총재(副總裁)들과 김녹영(金錄永) 의원(議員)을 초대(招待)를 했는데 이민우(李敏雨) 이기택(李基澤) 부총재(副總裁)만 와서 이이(*야)기 하다가 왔다. 한심한 일이다. 정말 불쌍하고 답답한 일이다.)

In the morning, I received a call from a Korean broadcasting station in the U.S. for a live broadcast interview, which I did. After attending church during the day, I went to Hanbit Church in the afternoon—also called Galilee Church. It’s a church where families of the detained or political prisoners gather in concern. They welcomed me joyfully with tears. I greeted them and talked for a while. Particularly heartwarming was Mr. Hartmut Albruschat, a pastor from West Berlin, Germany, who is in charge of Asia for his church and visited Galilee Church. He showed special interest in human rights in Korea, knew me well, and mentioned me twice during his greetings. A truly grateful person. <<>>> About 30 people gathered, but I believe it was more valuable and meaningful than if 3,000 had gathered. What a wonderful meeting it was! (아침에 미국(美囗)의 한국방송국에서 생방송(生放送)으로 나가는 전화가 와서 대담(對談)을 해주었다. 낮에 교회에 다녀와서 오후(午后)에 한빛교회에 나갔다. 일명(名) 갈리리 교회라고도 한다. 구속자 가족 또는 양심(良心)범 가족(家族)들이 모여서 걱정하며 모이는 교회이다. 정말 눈물로써 반가워 한다. 인사(人事)들을 하고 한참 이야기들을 했다. 특(特)히 반가운 것은 서독(西獨)에 있는 서(西)백림에 있는 교회(敎會)의 목사로써(*서) 아세아 담당으로 갈리리 교회(敎會)에 들여(*려)서 한국(韓囗)의 인권(人權)에 대(対)해서 특별(特別)한 관심(關心)을 보이며 나에 대해서 잘 알며 인사(人事)의 말하는 가운데 두 번이나 나에 대(対)한 이야기를 했다. Mr Hartmut ALbruschat이다. 고마운 사람이다.)

A secret letter arrived from Professor Han Wan-sang in the U.S. Its content is excellent. This is only possible when everyone casts aside selfish motives and moves forward together. (약(約)30명(名)의 사람들이 모였지마는 3000명(名)이 모인 것보다 가치(價値)가 있고 훌륭한 일이라고 생각한다. 얼마나 훌륭한 모임인가 말이다.)

item.title: Despite Two Task Forces Finding No Issues with ‘Audit of Moon’s Statistics Manipulation’, the Board of Audit and Inspection Continues Investigation Indefinitely (2차례 TF에도 ‘文 통계조작 감사’ 문제 못 찾자… 될 때까지 조사한다는 감사원)
item.description:
Despite Two Task Forces Finding No Issues with ‘Audit of Moon’s Statistics Manipulation’, the Board of Audit and Inspection Continues Investigation Indefinitely (2차례 TF에도 ‘文 통계조작 감사’ 문제 못 찾자… 될 때까지 조사한다는 감사원)

The Board of Audit and Inspection (BAI) has indefinitely extended the operational period of an internal task force (TF) investigating whether there were problems with the ‘audit into allegations of statistics manipulation under the Moon Jae-in government’ conducted during the Yoon Suk Yeol administration. Last year, the ‘Operational Reform TF’ spent about two months investigating this audit team and found no issues. Now, with the second TF launched at the end of April this year also failing to produce results within the initially planned three-month period, the deadline has been extended. Within the BAI, criticism is mounting, with some calling it “a rain dance-style investigation that keeps probing until the desired outcome is achieved.” (감사원이 윤석열 정부 시절 이뤄진 ‘문재인 정부 통계 조작 의혹 감사’에 문제가 있었는지 조사하는 내부 태스크포스(TF) 활동 기한을 무기한 연장했다. 지난해 ‘운영 쇄신 TF’에서 약 2개월간 이 감사팀을 조사하고도 아무 문제를 찾지 못했는데, 올해 4월 말 출범한 두 번째 TF도 지금까지 결과를 내놓지 못하자 당초 3개월로 예정한 활동 기한을 늘린 것이다. 감사원 내에서는 “원하는 결과가 나올 때까지 조사를 거듭하는 인디언 기우제식 조사를 한다”는 비판이 나온다.)

On the 9th, the BAI internally announced that the ‘Follow-up TF for the Special Committee on National Audit’ investigating the statistics manipulation audit team would extend its activity period from the originally scheduled end of this month to “until the conclusion of the work.” Such an indefinite investigation is unusual, even when auditing external agencies, which typically have set deadlines. (감사원은 지난 9일 통계 조작 의혹 감사팀을 조사하는 ‘국조특위 후속 조치 TF’의 활동 기한을 당초 예정한 이달 말에서 “업무 종료 시까지”로 연장한다고 내부에 공지했다. 피감 기관을 감사할 때에도 기한을 정해놓기에 이런 무기한 조사는 이례적이다.)

Within the BAI, there are murmurs that “the conservative camp likely wants a result showing the statistics manipulation audit was fundamentally flawed, and this extension may be due to the investigation results falling short of that.” Some also argue that under the Public Audit Act, an internal disciplinary investigation requires the inclusion of the regular inspection department, the Inspection Officer’s Office, but they have been excluded, raising questions about the legality of the TF’s activities. (감사원 내에서는 “여권에서는 통계 조작 감사가 근본적으로 잘못됐다는 결과를 원할 텐데, 조사 결과가 그에 못 미치기 때문 아니냐”는 말이 나온다. 공공감사법에 따라 기관 내부 감찰을 하려면 TF에 정규 감찰 부서인 감찰담당관실이 포함돼야 하는데 이들이 배제돼, TF 활동 자체에 위법 소지가 있다는 주장도 제기된다.)

In April last year, the BAI released an audit report claiming that the Moon government had manipulated and distorted statistics on housing, income, and employment over most of its five-year term. Former high-ranking officials from the Moon administration and the Democratic Party of Korea argued that BAI auditors had coercively investigated staff from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and the Korea Real Estate Board to fabricate a false audit report. (감사원은 지난해 4월 문 정부가 5년 임기 대부분 기간에 걸쳐 주택·소득·고용에 관한 통계를 조작·왜곡했다는 내용의 감사 보고서를 공개했다. 문 정부 고위 인사들과 더불어민주당은 감사원 감사관들이 국토부와 부동산원 직원들을 강압적으로 조사해 가짜 감사 보고서를 만들어낸 것이라고 주장했다.)

After the inauguration of the Lee Jae-myung government in September last year, the BAI formed an ‘Operational Reform TF’ with around 40 members to investigate the auditors who conducted the seven audits that the Democratic Party had questioned. The Moon government statistics manipulation audit team was among those investigated. However, even after a thorough review of 23,677 pages of evidence documents, over 1,000 minutes of audio recordings, and more than 5,100 minutes of video footage from the auditors’ Q&A sessions with ministry and real estate board staff, the TF found no issues with the statistics manipulation audit. (이재명 정부 출범 후인 지난해 9월 감사원은 40여 명 규모의 ‘운영 쇄신 TF’를 구성해, 민주당이 문제 삼은 감사 7건을 수행한 감사관들을 조사했다. 문 정부 통계 조작 의혹 감사팀도 이때 조사를 받았다. 그러나 TF는 증거 서류 2만3677쪽과 녹음 파일 1000여 분, 감사관들이 국토부·부동산원 직원들을 문답 조사할 때 녹화한 영상 5100여 분 등을 전수 조사하고도 통계 조작 의혹 감사의 문제점을 찾지 못했다.)

On April 28, the Democratic Party repeated its claims of coercive investigations during the statistics manipulation audit in a parliamentary inquiry into the ‘allegations of fabricated indictments.’ In response, the BAI reassembled a 30-member ‘Follow-up TF for the Special Committee on National Audit’ on the same day, tasking it with a focused review of only the statistics manipulation audit team. (민주당은 지난 4월 28일 ‘조작 기소 의혹’에 관한 국정조사에서 통계 조작 의혹 감사 중 강압 조사가 있었다는 주장을 되풀이했다. 그러자 감사원은 그날부로 30명을 동원한 ‘국조특위 후속 조치 TF’를 다시 만들어 통계 조작 감사팀만 집중적으로 들여다보게 했다.)

item.title: [Exclusive] U.S. Think Tank: "Lee Jae-myung Government's Nuclear Strategy is Passive but Ambitious" ([단독] 美 싱크탱크 “이재명 정부 핵 전략, 소극적이지만 야망 품어”)
item.description:
[Exclusive] U.S. Think Tank: "Lee Jae-myung Government's Nuclear Strategy is Passive but Ambitious" ([단독] 美 싱크탱크 “이재명 정부 핵 전략, 소극적이지만 야망 품어”)

In a recently released report, the U.S.-based think tank National Bureau of Asian Research (NBR) analyzed that the Lee Jae-myung administration's nuclear strategy shows "no intention of nuclear weaponization," yet harbors "entrepreneurial ambition" for nuclear potential, including uranium enrichment and spent nuclear fuel reprocessing technologies. It argued that while adhering to the U.S. nuclear umbrella protection framework, it is quietly pursuing independent nuclear capabilities. (미국 싱크탱크 아시아정책연구소(NBR)가 최근 공개한 보고서에서 이재명 정부의 핵 전략에 대해 “핵무기화 의도가 없다”면서도 우라늄 농축과 사용 후 핵연료 재처리 기술 등 핵 잠재력에 대한 “기업가적 야망(ambition)”이 깃들어 있다는 분석을 내놨다. 미국의 ‘핵우산’ 보호 체계를 따르면서도, 독자적인 핵 능력을 조용하게 추구하고 있다는 것이다.)

The report, titled 'Extended Deterrence in the Indo-Pacific' and released last month, addressed the nuclear strategies of South Korea, Japan, and Australia as separate subtopics. For South Korea, it provided a detailed 14-page analysis of recent nuclear strategy debates under the subtitle 'Dissecting the Nuclear Potential Debate in South Korea.' (지난달 공개된 ‘인도 태평양에서의 확장 억제’란 제목의 이 보고서는 한국, 일본, 호주의 핵 전략을 각각의 소주제로 다뤘다. 한국에 대해선 ‘한국의 핵 잠재력 논쟁 해부’라는 소제목하에 최근 한국에서 진행되고 있는 핵 전략 논의를 14페이지에 걸쳐 상세히 분석했다.)

The report first categorized South Korea's nuclear debaters into four types: ▲Nuclear Passivists, ▲Nuclear Negotiators, ▲Nuclear Entrepreneurs, and ▲Nuclear Opportunists. This classification was based on two criteria: 'How strong is the will to develop independent nuclear capabilities?' and 'How much risk is one willing to take in that process?' (보고서는 우선 한국의 핵 관련 논쟁가들을 ▲핵 소극파 ▲핵 협상파 ▲핵 기업가파 ▲핵 기회주의파 등 4가지 유형으로 나눴다. ‘자체 핵 능력을 키우려는 의지가 얼마나 강한가’ ‘그 과정에서 위험을 얼마나 감수하려 하는가’의 2가지 기준에 따른 것이다.)

Nuclear Passivists have a weak will for nuclear capability and are risk-averse. They trust the U.S. nuclear umbrella and worry that South Korea's nuclear discussions might negatively impact the Korea-U.S. alliance. Nuclear Negotiators do not have a strong nuclear will but believe that advocacy for nuclear armament within South Korea can be leveraged favorably in negotiations with the U.S. and others. Nuclear Entrepreneurs have a strong will to build nuclear capabilities but seek to pursue this quietly and pragmatically. Finally, Nuclear Opportunists openly advocate for strengthening nuclear capabilities, taking a stance that if the Korea-U.S. alliance becomes overly transactional, they would push for an 'independent nuclear path.' (핵 소극파는 핵 능력에 대한 의지도 약하고, 위험도 기피하는 사람들이다. 미국의 핵우산을 신뢰하며, 한국의 핵 논의가 한미 동맹에 부정적 영향을 주지 않을지 우려한다. 핵 협상파는 핵 의지는 강하지 않지만, 한국 내 핵무장론이 미국 등과의 협상에서 유리하게 활용될 수 있다고 본다. 핵 기업가파는 핵 능력을 키우려는 의지는 강하지만, 이를 조용하게 실용적으로 추진하려 한다. 마지막으로 핵 기회주의파는 핵 능력 강화를 공개적으로 주장한다. 한미 동맹이 지나치게 거래적으로 변한다면 ‘독자 핵 노선’을 추진할 수 있다는 입장이다.)

The report noted that the Lee Jae-myung administration simultaneously exhibits traits of both 'Nuclear Passivists' and 'Nuclear Entrepreneurs.' It pointed out that in terms of being passive, President Lee Jae-myung has stated that South Korea's independent nuclear armament is "impossible" and emphasizes the importance of U.S. extended deterrence. However, it also characterized the administration as entrepreneurial in seeking to upgrade nuclear capabilities discreetly, to the extent possible without arousing suspicion from neighboring countries. (보고서는 이재명 정부는 ‘핵 소극파’와 ‘핵 기업가파’의 특성을 동시에 보인다고 지적했다. 우선 이재명 대통령이 한국의 자체 핵무장이 “불가능”하다고 말하고, 미국 확장 억제의 중요성을 강조한다는 면에서는 소극파적 특성을 보인다고 했다. 그러나 가능한 한 주변국의 의심을 받지 않는 선에서 핵 능력의 고도화를 추구한다는 점에서는 기업가파 성격을 띤다는 것이다.)

The report analyzed that this entrepreneurial style was prominent in South Korea's recent push to introduce nuclear-powered submarines (SSNs). "President Lee pressured the U.S. side, as part of a larger package related to SSN introduction, to grant broader fuel cycle rights—including spent nuclear fuel reprocessing and uranium enrichment," it stated. (보고서는 최근 한국의 원자력 추진 잠수함(원잠) 도입 추진에서 이 같은 기업가 스타일이 두드러졌다고 분석했다. “이 대통령이 원잠 도입과 관련된 더 큰 패키지의 일부로서, 사용 후 핵연료를 재처리하고 우라늄을 농축할 수 있는 더 광범위한 연료 주기 권한을 달라고 미국 측에 압박했다”는 것이다.)

The report described the Lee administration's SSN diplomacy as combining "passive-style assurances based on the alliance—with no intention of nuclear weaponization—and entrepreneurial-style ambition, reflecting long-term efforts to negotiate nuclear fuel cycle and supply contracts." (보고서는 이재명 정부의 원잠 외교는 “핵 무기화 의도가 없고 (한미) 동맹에 기초한 소극파 스타일의 보장”과 “핵 연료 주기 및 공급 계약을 협상하는 장기적 지평의 노력을 뜻하는 기업가파 스타일의 야망”을 결합하고 있다고 했다.)

Jo Bi-yeon, a research fellow at the Sejong Institute who co-authored the report and wrote the section on South Korea's nuclear strategy, told this newspaper in a phone interview, "In recent SSN negotiations with the U.S., discussions have included South Korea receiving low-enriched uranium fuel from the U.S., but the government appears to be also considering long-term plans to domestically enrich fuel for SSNs. This reflects the 'nuclear entrepreneur' trait of quietly pursuing enhanced nuclear capabilities." However, she explained that by focusing on low-enriched fuel rather than high-enriched uranium, South Korea does not deviate from the international non-proliferation framework. (보고서의 공동 저자로서 한국 핵 전략 부분을 작성한 조비연 세종연구소 연구위원은 본지 통화에서 “최근 미국과의 원잠 협상에서 한국이 미국의 저농축 핵연료를 공급받는 방안이 논의되고 있지만, 정부는 장기적으로 원잠용 핵 연료도 한국에서 자체 농축하는 방안도 염두에 두는 것으로 보인다”며 “조용히 핵 능력 증진을 추구하는 ‘핵 기업가’적 특성을 나타내는 것”이라고 말했다. 다만 고농축 핵연료가 아닌 저농축 연료에 집중하면서 국제 사회의 ‘핵 비확산’ 기조를 벗어나진 않는다는 설명이다.)

In related developments, the foreign ministers of South Korea, the U.S., and Japan signed a 'Memorandum of Cooperation (MOC) on the Deployment of Small Modular Reactors (SMRs)' in Turkey on the 7th. The initiative aims for the three countries to jointly develop a single SMR model and deploy it across multiple nations, rather than each pursuing separate SMR projects. While this MOC is not directly related to South Korea's uranium enrichment or spent nuclear fuel reprocessing rights, it is seen as potentially serving as an opportunity to expand South Korea's civilian nuclear fuel enrichment rights. (이와 관련, 한·미·일 외교장관은 지난 7일 튀르키예에서 ‘소형 모듈 원자로(SMR) 배치에 관한 협력 각서(MOC)’를 체결했다. 한·미·일 3국이 제각기 SMR 사업에 뛰어들기보다, 하나의 SMR 모델을 개발한 뒤 여러 나라에 공동으로 보급하자는 취지다. 이번 MOC가 한국의 우라늄 농축이나 사용 후 핵연료 재처리 권한과 직접적 관련이 있는 것은 아니지만, 한국의 민수용 핵연료 농축 권한을 확대시킬 계기로 작용할 수 있다는 분석이 나오고 있다.)

Meanwhile, it is reported that after discussions in Seoul last month on expanding uranium enrichment and spent nuclear fuel reprocessing rights, along with SSN construction issues, South Korea and the U.S. are coordinating plans to hold a second round of consultations in the U.S. (한편 한·미 양국은 지난달 서울에서 우라늄 농축, 사용 후 핵연료 재처리 권한 확대와 원잠 건조 문제를 논의한 데 이어, 미국에서 2차 협의를 여는 방안을 조율하고 있는 것으로 알려졌다.)

item.title: President Lee to Hold Citizen-Participatory Work Reports Starting Tomorrow (李대통령, 내일부터 국민참여 업무보고)
item.description:
The presidential office announced on the 14th that President Lee Jae-myung will receive work reports from each ministry starting with the Ministry of Economy and Finance on the 15th, held nine times under the theme of 'An Irreplaceable Republic of Korea Experienced in Daily Life.' This marks the second round of work reports since his inauguration. During the first round of reports conducted at the end of last year, it was planned to check whether the contents reported by each ministry were being properly implemented. (이재명 대통령이 15일부터 재정경제부를 시작으로 9차례에 걸쳐 ‘삶으로 체감하는 대체 불가 대한민국’이라는 주제로 각 부처 업무 보고를 받는다고 청와대가 14일 밝혔다. 업무 보고는 취임 후 두 번째다. 지난 연말 진행한 첫 업무 보고 당시 각 부처의 보고 내용이 제대로 이행되고 있는지 점검할 예정이다.)

The total list of reporting agencies includes the Office for Government Policy Coordination, 19 ministries, 6 agencies, 18 offices, and 7 committees, along with 140 public institutions pursuing citizen-experienced livelihood projects. On the first day, the 15th, starting at 10 AM, the Ministry of Economy and Finance (including the National Tax Service, Korea Customs Service, and Public Procurement Service), the National Data Agency, the Financial Services Commission, and the Ministry of Strategy and Finance will conduct reports for about 100 minutes. (전체 보고 대상 기관은 국무조정실과 19부 6처 18청 7위원회를 포함해 국민 체감형 민생 사업을 추진하는 140개 공공기관이다. 이 중 첫날인 15일에는 오전 10시부터 재정경제부(국세청·관세청·조달청), 국가데이터처, 금융위원회, 기획예산처가 약 100분간 보고를 진행한다.)

On the following day, the 16th, in the morning, work reports will be held by the Ministry of Science and ICT (including the Korea AeroSpace Administration), the Broadcasting and Media Communication Commission, and the Personal Information Protection Commission. At 2 PM on the same day, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (including the Administrative City Construction Agency and the Saemangeum Development Agency), the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (including the Rural Development Administration and the Korea Forest Service), and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (including the Korea Coast Guard) will report. Starting at 4:20 PM, the Ministry of Health and Welfare (including the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency), the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family, and the Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission will take turns reporting. Work reports for other ministries are scheduled to take place in early August. (이튿날인 16일 오전에는 과학기술정보통신부(우주항공청)·방송미디어통신위원회·개인정보보호위원회의 업무 보고가 이뤄진다. 같은 날 오후 2시에는 국토교통부(행정중심복합도시건설청·새만금개발청)·농림축산식품부(농촌진흥청·산림청)·해양수산부(해양경찰청)가, 오후 4시 20분부터는 보건복지부(질병관리청)·식품의약품안전처·성평등가족부·국민권익위원회가 차례로 업무보고에 나선다. 그 외 부처의 업무보고는 8월 초에 진행될 예정이다.)

For this round of work reports, about 20 citizens per session, totaling around 200 people, will attend as a citizen participation group. The presidential office previously recruited applicants via social media, and the competition ratio was approximately 6.3 to 1, according to the office's explanation. (이번 업무 보고에는 매회 약 20여 명씩 모두 200여 명의 국민참여단이 현장을 찾는다. 앞서 청와대는 SNS를 통해 신청자를 모집했고 경쟁률은 약 6.3대 1이었다고 청와대는 설명했다.)

item.title: Chung Pointsung: "People Power Party Threatens to Monopolize Committees... If That's What They Want, Amend the National Assembly Act and Take Them" (정점식 “與, 상임위 독식 협박...원하면 국회법 개정해 가져가라”)
item.description:
As the People Power Party boycotts amid the Democratic Party of Korea's unilateral committee formation, People Power Party floor leader Chung Pointsung said on the 14th, "If they can only be satisfied by taking all 18 standing committees, then let them take them all." (국민의힘이 더불어민주당의 일방적 상임위 구성에 반발하며 보이콧을 하고 있는 가운데 국민의힘 정점식 원내대표는 14일 “18개 상임위를 다 가져가야만 직성이 풀린다면 다 가져가라”고 했다.)

Floor leader Chung stated at a floor strategy meeting held at the National Assembly in Yeouido, Seoul, that morning, "Instead, go ahead and unilaterally amend the National Assembly Act so that the largest party in the chamber monopolizes the chairmanship of all 18 standing committees and take them." (정 원내대표는 이날 오전 서울 여의도 국회에서 열린 원내대책회의에서 “대신 아예 원내 제1당이 18개 상임위원장직을 독식한다고 국회법을 단독 개정하고 가져가라”고 했다.)

He criticized the Democratic Party, saying, "The Democratic Party is repeatedly using threatening media tactics to claim they will take all 18 standing committees," and added, "Stop deceiving the public by pretending negotiations between the ruling and opposition parties exist through threats that are not negotiations or pointless stalling." (그는 민주당을 향해 “민주당이 18개 상임위를 모두 가져가겠다는 협박성 언론 플레이를 반복하고 있다”며 “더 이상 협상 아닌 협박 또는 무의미한 시간 끌기로 여야 간의 협상이 존재하는 것처럼 국민을 속이지 말라”고 했다.)

The People Power Party's boycott of standing committees has now entered its second week. Floor leader Chung held a meeting of senior lawmakers and a general meeting of party lawmakers the previous day to gather their opinions. It was reported that at these meetings, People Power Party lawmakers reached a consensus to maintain the policy of a full boycott of National Assembly standing committees. (국민의힘의 상임위 보이콧은 2주째 계속되고 있다. 정 원내대표는 전날 중진 간담회와 의원총회를 연달아 열고 의원들의 의견을 들었다. 이 자리에서 국민의힘 의원들은 국회 상임위 전면 보이콧 방침을 유지하는 데 공감대를 이룬 것으로 전해졌다.)

Floor leader Chung met with reporters after a meeting with 12 senior lawmakers the previous morning and said, "The general sentiment is whether it even makes sense to enter into negotiations over the formation of committees under the current circumstances," and added, "I think the views of the senior lawmakers and other lawmakers are likely to be largely aligned." (정 원내대표는 전날 오전 중진 의원 12명과 간담회 이후 기자들과 만나 “대체적 생각은 원 구성 협상도 지금 같은 상황에 들어가는 게 맞냐는 것”이라며 “중진들 생각과 다른 의원들 생각이 거의 일치하지 않을까 생각은 든다”고 말했다.)

item.title: Jjinjang, Muljang, Nyujang… Jang Dong-hyuk’s Faction Splits (찐장, 멀장, 뉴장… 장동혁 당권파도 분화)
item.description:
Jjinjang, Muljang, Nyujang… Jang Dong-hyuk’s Faction Splits (찐장, 멀장, 뉴장… 장동혁 당권파도 분화)

Amid ongoing concerns within the People Power Party about the leadership of its leader, Jang Dong-hyuk, his inner circle is also fragmenting. Party insiders refer to these groups as “Jjinjang,” “Muljang,” and “Nyujang.” <<>> “Jjinjang” refers to the innermost circle that has held party positions since Jang won the party leadership election in August last year and continues to share opinions with him. Representative Park Jun-tae, a proportional representative lawmaker serving as the party leader’s chief of staff, is a key figure. It is known that Jang has privately praised Park, calling him “a lawmaker who knows his role well and carries it out properly.” Also close to Jang are first-term Supreme Council member Shin Dong-wook, party leader’s political affairs office head Kim Jang-kyum, Deputy General Strategy Director Seo Cheon-ho, and Yoido Research Institute Director Jo Seung-hwan. A party insider noted, “After winning his seat in the 2022 by-election and serving as secretary-general, Jang tends to be closer to first-term lawmakers than to senior figures.” <<>> “Muljang” describes those whom Jang appointed to party positions but now keep their distance. Within the party, first-term lawmaker Kim Dae-sik is cited as an example. Kim was appointed chief of the party leader’s special advisory team and reportedly planned Jang’s visit to the United States ahead of local elections. However, he distanced himself from Jang after advocating for a unified candidacy with independent candidate Han Dong-hoon in the Busan North Gap by-election. Some lawmakers holding party positions have expressed concerns about Jang’s operational direction and have pulled back, with some even asking, “Please don’t refer to me as a close aide of Leader Jang.” <<>> There is also a newly emerging “Nyujang” group. These are individuals who actively defend Jang amid growing calls inside and outside the party for his resignation. They include first-term lawmakers Kim Min-jeon and Seo Myeong-ok, as well as Kim Tae-kyu and Lee Jin-sook, who entered the National Assembly through the June 3 by-election. Kim Min-jeon, who strongly opposed the impeachment of former President Yoon Suk-yeol, reportedly defended Jang at a recent People Power Party lawmakers’ meeting and posted similar messages in the party’s group chat on Telegram. On the 13th, Lee Jin-sook appeared on CBS Radio and, regarding calls for Jang’s resignation, stated, “It’s right to let the party leader serve out his term.” Jang’s term runs until August next year. <<>> The majority of lawmakers from Daegu and North Gyeongsang Province, who form the party’s mainstream, are taking a wait-and-see stance and have not voiced strong opinions. While they agree that the party cannot face the 2028 general election under Jang’s leadership, they also see no viable alternative if Jang steps down immediately. A first-term lawmaker with weak factional ties commented, “I thought Jang’s leadership would collapse quickly, but since he’s holding on with party member support, aren’t the lawmakers also being cautious?” (국민의힘 장동혁 대표 리더십에 대한 당내 우려가 계속되는 가운데 장 대표 측근 그룹도 분화하고 있다. 당 관계자들은 이들을 ‘찐장’ ‘멀장’ ‘뉴장’ 등으로 부르고 있다.)

item.title: 11 Lawmakers from the Ruling Party Propose Bill to Keep Supplementary Investigation Powers, Saying "Disadvantaged Must Be Protected" (與 의원 11명, 보완수사권 완전 폐지 ‘반대’ 법안 발의…“사회적 약자 보호해야”)
item.description:
While the Democratic Party of Korea is moving quickly to completely abolish the prosecution's supplementary investigation powers, 11 lawmakers, led by party member Hong Ki-won, have proposed a bill to retain some of these powers. (더불어민주당이 검찰의 보완수사권을 전면 폐지하는 데 속도를 내는 가운데, 당내 홍기원 의원을 중심으로 11명의 의원이 보완수사권의 일부를 존치하는 내용의 법안을 발의했다.)

On the 14th, Rep. Hong held a press conference at the National Assembly Communication Center before proposing the amendment to the Criminal Procedure Act. The lawmakers who co-signed the amendment included, besides Hong, Ko Min-jung, Kwak Sang-eon, Kim Nam-hee, Mo Kyung-jong, Moon Jin-seok, Min Hong-chul, Park Kyun-taek, Park Hee-seung, Lee So-young, and Joo Cheol-hyun. (14일 홍 의원은 국회 소통관에서 형사소송법 개정안을 발의하기 전 기자회견을 열었다. 개정안 공동발의자에 이름을 올린 의원은 홍 의원 외 고민정·곽상언·김남희·모경종·문진석·민홍철·박균택·박희승·이소영·주철현 의원이었다.)

Rep. Hong stated, "Many lawmakers lacked time for review, which is why not many participated. There were also those who agreed with the bill's content but said they couldn't participate as co-sponsors due to their party positions." He added, "Some said they share the intent but couldn't co-sponsor because it might affect the party convention." (홍 의원은 “여러 의원들께서 검토할 시간이 부족했기 떄문에 많이 참여 못한 측면이 있다. 또 법안 내용에 공감은 하는데 본인이 당직을 맡고 있어서 공동발의에는 참여하기 어렵다고 말한 분도 계셨다”고 했다. 또 “전당대회에 영향 미칠 수도 있기 때문에 뜻은 같이하지만 공동 발의는 못하겠다는 분도 있었다”고 했다.)

Rep. Hong cited cases where exceptional supplementary investigation by the prosecution is necessary, including crimes against socially disadvantaged groups, crimes harming people's livelihoods, urgent cases like detention with tight deadlines, cases requiring consolidation or where victims have filed objections, and minor incidents. (홍 의원은 검찰의 예외적 보완수사가 필요한 경우로 사회적 약자 대상 범죄, 민생 침해 범죄, 구속 사건 등 시한이 촉박한 경우, 사건 병합이 필요하거나 피해자가 이의 신청했을 경우, 내용이 경미한 때를 들었다.)

Meanwhile, later in the day, the Democratic Party will hold a general meeting of lawmakers to continue discussions on the Criminal Procedure Act. After gathering internal opinions, the party plans to proceed through the Legislation and Judiciary Committee subcommittee and general meeting on the 15th. item.title: Whistleblowers of Corruption to Receive 30% of Reported Amount as Reward (부정부패 신고자에게 신고액 30% 보상금으로 준다)
item.description:
The Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission is pushing for a plan to give whistleblowers 30% of the amount recovered when the state recovers revenue that was nearly lost due to corruption, through reports from citizens. It also seeks to abolish the reward cap, which was previously limited to 3 billion won. (국가가 부정부패로 잃어버릴 뻔한 수익을 국민의 신고로 회복하게 된 경우, 신고자에게 그 금액의 30%를 보상금으로 주는 방안을 국민권익위원회가 추진한다. 30억원으로 제한됐던 보상금 상한의 폐지도 추진된다.)

On the 14th, the Commission announced that it would pre-announce legislation for amendments to the enforcement decrees of the Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission Act, the Public Interest Whistleblower Protection Act, and the Public Finance Recovery Act, containing these provisions, from that day until the 24th of next month. During this period, the Commission will gather opinions from relevant ministries. General citizens can also submit their opinions through the National Participation Legislative Center (opinion.lawmaking.go.kr) and other channels. Once the amendments reflecting each opinion pass through a vice-ministerial meeting and are approved by the Cabinet, the enforcement decrees will be formally revised. (권익위는 14일 이러한 내용을 담은 부패방지권익위법 시행령과 공익신고자 보호법 시행령, 공공재정환수법 시행령 개정안을 이날부터 다음 달 24일까지 입법 예고한다고 밝혔다. 이 기간 동안 권익위는 개정안에 관해 관계 부처에서 의견을 수렴한다. 일반 국민도 국민참여입법센터(opinion.lawmaking.go.kr) 등을 통해 의견을 낼 수 있다. 각 의견을 반영한 개정안이 차관회의를 거쳐 국무회의를 통과하면 시행령들이 실제로 개정된다.)

Currently, there is a differential reward rate depending on the amount of revenue the state has recovered. If the recovered amount is 1 billion won or less, 30% is given as a reward. However, for portions between 1 billion and 5 billion won, it is 20%; between 5 billion and 20 billion won, 14%; between 20 billion and 40 billion won, 8%; and for amounts exceeding 40 billion won, only 4% is given. This creates a structure where the reward rate decreases as the contribution of the corruption whistleblower increases. (현재는 국가가 수입을 회복한 금액이 얼마인지에 따라 보상 비율에 차등이 있다. 수입 회복 금액이 1억원 이하일 때는 30%를 보상금으로 주지만, 1억~5억원 부분에 대해서는 20%, 5억~20억원 부분에 대해서는 14%, 20억~40억원 부분에 대해서는 8%, 40억원을 초과하는 부분에 대해서는 4%만 준다. 부정부패 신고자의 공헌이 클수록 보상 비율이 낮아지는 구조다.)

The Commission decided to eliminate this differentiation and provide 30% as a reward regardless of the amount of revenue recovered. It also decided to abolish the reward cap, which was applied differently depending on the type of report. Currently, there is no cap on rewards for 'public interest reports,' but for 'corruption reports' or reports of violations of the Public Finance Recovery Act, the reward is limited to a maximum of 3 billion won. The plan is to remove this distinction. (권익위는 이런 차등을 없애고, 수입 회복 금액이 얼마인지와 상관없이 30%를 보상금으로 주기로 했다. 또 신고의 종류에 따라 달리 적용되던 보상금 상한도 폐지하기로 했다. 지금은 ‘공익 신고’를 한 경우에는 보상금에 상한이 없지만, ‘부패 신고’나 공공재정환수법 위반 신고를 한 경우에는 보상금이 최대 30억원으로 제한되는데, 이 구분을 없애겠다는 것이다.)

Consequently, rewards for those who report large-scale corruption cases will increase significantly. For example, someone reporting a 10 billion won corruption case would currently receive only 720 million won as a reward, but if the new enforcement decree passes, they would be able to receive 3 billion won. (이에 따라, 대규모 부정부패 사건을 신고한 사람에 대한 보상금이 크게 늘어난다. 예를 들어, 100억원 규모의 부정부패를 신고한 사람이라면 보상금으로 지금은 7억2000만원만 받아갈 수 있지만, 새 시행령이 통과되면 30억원을 받아갈 수 있게 된다.)

The Commission stated, however, that it will maintain the current deduction criteria for evaluating the whistleblower’s contribution. Rewards will be reduced if the reported content is inaccurate or the credibility of evidence is somewhat low, if the reported information has already been disclosed through the media, if the whistleblower themselves was involved in the illegal act, or if the whistleblower had an initial duty to report. This will remain the same going forward. (권익위는 다만 신고자의 공헌도를 평가하는 감액 기준은 지금처럼 유지하겠다고 했다. 신고 내용이 부정확하거나 증거 자료의 신빙성이 다소 낮은 경우, 신고한 내용이 언론을 통해 이미 공개된 내용인 경우, 신고자 본인도 불법행위에 가담한 경우, 신고자에게 애초에 신고 의무가 있는 경우에는 보상금이 감액되는데, 이는 앞으로도 마찬가지라는 것이다.)

Vice Chairperson Lee Myung-soon of the Anti-Corruption Bureau at the Commission said, “This amendment to the enforcement decree is meaningful in reorganizing the reward system so that citizens who bravely report for the public interest receive compensation commensurate with their contribution,” adding, “We will continue to improve the protection and reward systems so that citizens can report with peace of mind.” (권익위 이명순 부패방지 담당 부위원장은 “이번 시행령 개정은 공익을 위해 용기 있게 신고한 국민이 그 기여에 상응하는 보상을 받을 수 있도록 보상 체계를 정비하는 데 의미가 있다”며 “앞으로도 국민이 안심하고 신고할 수 있도록 보호·보상 제도를 지속적으로 개선해 나가겠다”고 했다.)

item.title: Jung Cheong-rae: "We Were Criticized for Boosting Cho Kuk, But Shouldn't Have Run a Candidate in Pyeongtaek B" (정청래 “조국 키운다 공격 받았겠지만, 평택乙 후보 안 냈어야”)
item.description:
Jung Cheong-rae, a candidate for the leadership of the Democratic Party of Korea, stated on the 14th regarding the loss in the by-election for Pyeongtaek B, held alongside the June 3 local elections, "Looking back now, I think it would have been right for the Democratic Party not to field a candidate." (더불어민주당 당권 주자인 정청래 전 대표는 14일 지난 6·3 지방선거와 함께 치러진 경기 평택을 국회의원 재선거 패배와 관련해 “지금 되돌아보면 민주당이 후보를 내지 않는 게 맞지 않았을까 생각한다”고 말했다.)

Appearing on Kim Eo-jun's YouTube broadcast that day, Jung explained, "At the time, when the Rebuilding Korea Party said the Democratic Party shouldn't run a candidate, we couldn't say, 'We won't field one.' I believed it was the party leader's duty to run candidates in all districts and do our best to win." (정 전 대표는 이날 김어준씨의 유튜브 방송에 출연해 “당시에는 조국혁신당에서 민주당 후보를 내지 말라고 했을 때 ‘안 내겠다’고 할 수는 없었다”며 “전 지역에 후보를 내고 최선을 다해 승리하는 것이 당대표로서 당연한 의무라고 생각했다”고 밝혔다.)

He added, "In the end, it resulted in handing a seat to the People Power Party through a fluke. I also wonder what might have happened if the merger had succeeded before the June 3 local elections." (그는 “결과적으로는 어부지리로 국민의힘에 한 석을 넘겨준 상황이 됐다”며 “6·3 지방선거 전에 합당이 성공했다면 어땠을까 하는 생각도 많이 하게 된다”고 했다.)

In the Pyeongtaek B by-election, former lawmaker Kim Yong-nam, a prosecutor-turned-politician who served in the 19th National Assembly under the Saenuri Party, the predecessor of the People Power Party, was strategically nominated as the Democratic Party candidate. Kim ran as the People Power Party candidate for Suwon mayor in 2022, then left the party in 2024 to join the Reform Party, later entering the Democratic Party during the last presidential election as part of President Lee Jae-myung's move to expand integration and outreach. Rebuilding Korea Party leader Cho Kuk also ran, but the two candidates failed to unify, leading to the election of the People Power Party's Yoo Eui-dong. (평택을 재선거에는 검사 출신으로 국민의힘 전신인 새누리당에서 19대 국회의원을 지낸 김용남 전 의원이 민주당 후보로 전략공천됐다. 김 전 의원은 2022년 국민의힘 수원시장 후보로 출마했고, 2024년 국민의힘을 탈당해 개혁신당에 합류했다가 지난 대선 당시 이재명 대통령의 통합·외연 확장 인사로 민주당에 입당했다. 조국혁신당에서는 조국 대표가 출마했지만 두 후보의 단일화가 무산됐고, 국민의힘 유의동 후보가 당선됐다.)

Jung explained that if the Democratic Party hadn't fielded a candidate then, internal criticism against him would have been fierce. He said, "If we had done that, I would have faced criticism and attacks, like, 'Isn't Jung Cheong-rae, as party leader, trying to boost Cho Kuk?' or 'This is a revival of the pro-Moon faction.' There would have been much confusion and division, but if we had done that, the outcome might have been different." (정 전 대표는 당시 민주당이 후보를 내지 않았다면 자신을 향한 당내 비판도 거셌을 것이라고 설명했다. 그는 “그렇게 했으면 ‘정청래 당대표가 조국을 키워주려고 하는 것 아니냐’, ‘친문 부활이 맞다’는 비난과 공격을 받았을 것”이라며 “많은 혼란과 분열도 있었겠지만, 그렇게 했다면 결과는 달라졌을 것”이라고 말했다.)

He continued, "The pain is that you can't live life twice. At the time, we couldn't make that choice because of such attacks, but looking back now, I think we should have done it." He added, "Regarding the Pyeongtaek B election, I bear significant responsibility as the former party leader." (이어 “세상은 두 번 살지 못하는 것이 아픔”이라며 “당시에는 그런 공격 때문에 선택하지 못했지만, 지금 되돌아보면 그렇게 했어야 했던 것 같다”고 했다. 그러면서 “평택을 선거에 대해서는 당대표였던 제 책임이 크다고 본다”고 말했다.)

Reflecting on his judgment at the time, Jung said, "I think I was gripped by the obsession that the most important duty of a party leader is to field candidates in all districts and win." He remarked, "At the time, I was deep in the intense campaign environment, but I should have looked at the overall situation from a broader perspective." (정 전 대표는 당시 판단에 대해 “모든 지역에 후보를 내고 이기는 것이 당대표의 가장 중요한 책무라는 강박관념이 컸던 것 같다”고 돌아봤다. 그는 “당시에는 치열한 선거 현장 안에 들어가 있었지만, 전체 전황을 좀 더 멀리서 봤어야 했다”고 했다.)

He also acknowledged his responsibility for the failed merger with the Rebuilding Korea Party. Jung stated, "I wanted to propose and push for a merger, but there was strong opposition, and ultimately it failed. Regarding criticisms that the process was abrupt and rough, I admit I fell short, and that's my responsibility." (조국혁신당과의 합당이 무산된 데 대해서도 자신의 책임을 인정했다. 정 전 대표는 “합당을 제안하고 추진하고 싶었지만 강력한 반대가 있었고, 결과적으로 실패했다”며 “과정이 전격적이고 거칠었다는 지적에는 부족함이 있었고, 그 부분은 제 책임”이라고 말했다.)

However, he maintained that the need for integration between the Democratic Party and the Rebuilding Korea Party remains valid. Jung said, "If the goal is to win general and presidential elections and recreate the government, then outside the party, we need to integrate where integration is possible and form alliances where alliances are needed. Whether to merge should be first asked of the members of the Democratic Party and the Rebuilding Korea Party." (다만 그는 민주당과 조국혁신당의 통합 필요성은 여전히 유효하다는 입장을 밝혔다. 정 전 대표는 “총선과 대선 승리, 정권 재창출이 목표라면 당 밖으로는 통합할 곳은 통합하고 연대할 곳은 연대해야 한다”며 “합당 여부는 민주당과 조국혁신당 당원들에게 먼저 물어야 한다”고 했다.)

item.title: Government Announces Additional $3.5 Million in Humanitarian Aid for Venezuela Earthquake Relief (정부, 베네수엘라 강진 피해에 350만달러 추가 인도적 지원)
item.description:
The government announced on the 14th that it has decided to provide $3.5 million (approximately 5.2 billion won) in humanitarian aid, considering the continuously expanding scale of damage from the recent severe earthquake in Venezuela. This is an additional measure following the decision in late June to provide $5 million in humanitarian aid to Venezuela. (정부는 최근 베네수엘라에서 발생한 강진으로 피해 규모가 지속 확대되는 상황을 감안해 350만달러(약 52억원) 상당의 인도적 지원을 제공하기로 결정했다고 14일 밝혔다. 지난 6월 말 베네수엘라에 500만달러 규모의 인도적 지원을 결정한 데 이은 추가 조치다.)

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated, "Of this aid, $3 million will be used through the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) for debris removal activities to help residents quickly return to their daily lives." (외교부는 “이번 지원 중 300만달러는 유엔개발계획(UNDP)을 통해 주민들의 조속한 일상 복귀를 돕기 위한 잔해 제거 활동에 사용될 예정”이라고 밝혔다.)

In addition, in response to a request from the Venezuelan government, the government decided to provide in-kind support of 30 tons of temporary shelters (family tents), valued at $500,000, for accommodating displaced victims. (정부는 또 베네수엘라 정부의 요청에 따라 이재민 수용을 위한 30톤 분량(50만달러 상당)의 임시 거처(패밀리 텐트)도 현물 지원하기로 했다.)

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said, "We will continue to provide humanitarian aid to countries and people affected by natural disasters in the future." (외교부는 “앞으로도 자연재해로 피해를 본 국가와 국민들에 대한 인도적 지원을 계속해 나갈 예정”이라고 했다.)
